archetype.name: Pocket Passer (quick-game)
archetype.definition: A non-running pocket quarterback who, in Atlanta's run-first offense, has shortened his reads to quick and intermediate throws behind a line that rarely lets him get touched.

report.headline: Three efficient starts, a cleaner style, and a rib injury hanging over everything
report.take:
Penix took the job in Week 3 after Cooper Rush and Tua Tagovailoa started the first two games, and he has been the most efficient version of himself so far. His 9.34 yards per attempt ranks 2nd and his 0.343 EPA per dropback ranks 5th among 43 qualifiers. He is doing it on modest volume, about 26 attempts a game, in an offense that passes 9 points less often than situation predicts (29th) and leans on the league's 3rd-best rushing attack. He offers nothing as a runner: 4 yards on 6 carries.

The style has changed. Last season he averaged an 8.9-yard aDOT with a 14.9% aggressiveness rate, and his bad-throw rate ranked 59th of 63, as it had the year before. This year his intended air yards are down to 6.95, aggressiveness is 7.79%, and his bad-throw rate is 5.2% (2nd). He is getting the ball out in 2.55 seconds behind a line that has him pressured on 3.8% of dropbacks, fewest in the league. The damage comes from the intermediate zone, where he has 0.868 EPA on 20 throws, and from Drake London, who is drawing 25 targets at 1.128 EPA each.

The numbers flatter him in two ways. Two of his three starts were 35-14 and 45-24 blowouts, and his 18 dropbacks with a lead of 9 or more produced 1.177 EPA per play. On the 64 dropbacks within one score he is at 0.104 with a -3.2 CPOE, which is good but not top-five. His career CPOE has been about -4 in both prior seasons, and the tracking CPOE this year is -0.5, so the accuracy jump is partly the product of easier throws. The deep numbers (2.65 EPA, 83% completions) rest on six attempts and won't hold.

The immediate question is health. He left the Baltimore loss with a rib injury, played 95% of snaps, and was set for an MRI. He is listed questionable with an estimated return date of game day. Ribs tend to show up in velocity and in how a quarterback takes hits, and his 33.3% pressure-to-sack rate (30th) means the rare pressure he does face often ends in a sack.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws and third downs
strengths.body: His best work is between 10 and 19 yards, and on third down, where he converts 51.9% of the time despite 7.2 yards to go on average. This is the area that rewards timing and decisiveness more than arm strength. It is the most sustainable part of his profile, though 20 intermediate throws is still a small sample.

strengths.title: Clean pockets, cleaner footwork
strengths.body: He is pressured on 3.8% of dropbacks, best in the league, behind an offense that ranks 2nd in hit rate allowed. His bad-throw rate has collapsed from about 22% in each prior season to 5.2%. Some of that is the shorter target depth and the protection, not a remade passer. It should hold as long as the line and the quick-game design do.

strengths.title: Drake London as the engine
strengths.body: London has 25 of the targets and 1.128 EPA per target, more than double anyone else's volume. Kyle Pitts adds a second efficient option at 0.806 per target. Concentration like this is repeatable because it reflects the read structure, though the per-target efficiency will come down.

concerns.title: Rib injury with a sack-prone profile
concerns.body: He exited the Ravens game and is questionable after an MRI. Even if he plays, a rib injury can sap his throwing and make the hits hurt. That matters more because a third of his pressures have ended in sacks, and the three sacks against Baltimore were his most in any start.

concerns.title: Efficiency padded by blowouts
concerns.body: His 0.343 EPA per dropback is lifted by 18 dropbacks with a big lead. In one-score situations he is at 0.104 with negative CPOE, close to his 2025 baseline of 0.079 EPA per play. His career CPOE has been about -4 in both prior seasons. Expect the overall number to drift toward the one-score figure.

concerns.title: Screens and red zone drag
concerns.body: Of his 77 attempts, 24 have been behind the line, at -0.441 EPA with a -21.9 CPOE, so the screen game is a drain. Inside the 20 he is 4-of-12 for two touchdowns. Both are small samples, but combined with a run-first call sheet they cap his touchdown and yardage ceiling.

trend.note: Each start produced between 223 and 256 yards with one touchdown, and his EPA was positive every week (9.5, 10.6, 7.6). Baltimore was the least clean game: a -5 CPOE, three sacks and more aggressive throws in a one-score loss before the rib injury.

nextGame.headline: Bears bleed deep but choke the short game he lives in
nextGame.body:
Chicago's defense is middling overall (20th in EPA) but extreme by depth. It ranks 2nd against short passes and 32nd against deep ones, and allows the 30th-ranked explosive pass rate. That is an awkward fit for a quarterback who has thrown 51 of his 77 passes short or behind the line and only six deep. The way in is the run game: the Bears are 27th against the run, and Atlanta's 3rd-ranked ground attack should set up the intermediate play-action shots where Penix has been best. The catch is that a successful run plan also caps his attempts.

Availability matters on both sides. Penix is questionable with the rib injury, and if he can't go, everything here changes. On Chicago's side, Caleb Williams was out as of the last report, with Ben Johnson non-committal on a return. That bears on game script: a weaker Bears offense makes a run-heavy Falcons lead more likely. The Chicago secondary is thin. Kyler Gordon is out, safety Anthony Johnson Jr. is out, and corner Tyrique Stevenson (65% of snaps) is questionable. Linebacker T.J. Edwards and edge Dayo Odeyingbo are also questionable.

keyMatchups.title: London against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Chicago allows 0.58 EPA per play to opposing WR1s, 28th in the league. With Gordon out and Stevenson questionable, London's volume should translate. He is the most likely route to the explosive plays Chicago gives up.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game into Chicago's strength
keyMatchups.body: The Bears allow -0.207 EPA on short throws, 2nd-best. Penix's short game has been good (0.356 EPA), but this is the matchup most likely to stall it. That pushes the offense toward the run or the deeper throws he has rarely attempted.

keyMatchups.title: Bijan-led run plan against a soft front
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta's rushing offense ranks 3rd in EPA, and Chicago's run defense ranks 27th, with RB1s scoring 3 PPR points over their averages against it. Expect the script to tilt toward the ground game, which helps the Falcons win but trims Penix's volume.

nextGame.watch: Whether Penix practices fully this week. If he does, his willingness to push throws past the sticks against Chicago's 32nd-ranked deep defense decides whether he beats his baseline.

restOfSeason.body:
Expect a productive but capped passer: roughly 25 to 30 attempts a game in a run-first offense, efficient enough to keep the job, with fewer blowout-padded dropbacks. The protection, the London concentration and the intermediate timing look real. The deep efficiency, the near-zero pressure rate and the sub-6% bad-throw rate will likely move toward normal, since his history includes two seasons of below-expected accuracy.

His EPA per dropback should settle somewhere between his 2025 level and this three-game burst, which would still make him a positive starter. The touchdown rate (3.9%) is not inflated, so scoring production should hold steady rather than regress. The rib injury is the biggest variable: a quarterback playing hurt behind a line that allows few hits but whose pressures often end in sacks.
swingFactors: Rib injury recovery and his practice status
Whether Atlanta keeps pass rate well below expected
Pass protection holding at its 2nd-ranked hit rate

bets.reason: Chicago is laying road points with Caleb Williams out as of the last report, a depleted secondary and a 27th-ranked run defense, against a Falcons team with the 7th-ranked defense and 3rd-ranked rushing offense. The bet assumes Penix plays; his rib status is the main reason the line sits where it does.

Chicago's short-pass defense ranks 2nd, which is where most of his attempts go. A soft Bears run defense invites Atlanta's already run-heavy script. A rib injury argues for fewer attempts and less push downfield.

confidence.note: Three starts, 84 dropbacks, and a rib injury.
